claim: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is projected to affect >280 million people worldwide by 2040.
source: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of blindness in the industrialised world and is projected to affect >280 million people worldwide by 2040.
evidence: This is a factual projection stated in the abstract without direct supporting data in the manuscript, likely drawing from established scientific knowledge or external sources.

claim: 44 traits were found to be putatively causal for early AMD in univariable analysis.
source: Overall, 44 traits were found to be putatively causal for early AMD in univariable analysis.
evidence: This claim is directly supported by the results of the univariable MR analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Genome-wide association studies have identified AMD-implicated variants in at least 69 loci.
source: genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified AMD-implicated variants in at least 69 loci. These include important risk alleles in the 1q32 and 10q26 genomic regions (corresponding to the CFH [complement factor H] and ARMS2/HTRA1 locus, respectively) (Fritsche et al., 2016; Winkler et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous GWAS studies.

claim: Important AMD risk alleles are located in the 1q32 and 10q26 genomic regions corresponding to the CFH and ARMS2/HTRA1 locus.
source: These include important risk alleles in the 1q32 and 10q26 genomic regions (corresponding to the CFH [complement factor H] and ARMS2/HTRA1 locus, respectively) (Fritsche et al., 2016; Winkler et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous GWAS studies.

claim: Key AMD risk factors include age, smoking, alcohol consumption, and low dietary intake of antioxidants (carotenoids, zinc).

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Advanced AMD results in loss of central vision, often leading to severe visual impairment.

claim: AMD is a major cause of blindness in the elderly population.
source: Notably, AMD is a major cause of blindness in the elderly population and represents a substantial global burden that is expected to continue to grow into the future as an ageing population expands worldwide (Chakravarthy et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents established epidemiological knowledge.

claim: The early AMD GWAS meta-analysis included 14,034 early AMD cases and 91,214 controls overall.
source: This meta-analysis focussed on populations of European ancestries and used data from the ARIC, AugUR, CHS, GHS, IAMDGC, KORA S4, LIFE-Adult NICOLA, UKBB, and WHI studies (14,034 early AMD cases and 91,214 controls overall).
evidence: This is a description of the data source used in the study, citing the Winkler et al., 2020 meta-analysis.

claim: The advanced AMD GWAS included data from IAMDGC 2013 (17,181 cases and 60,074 controls), IAMDGC 2016 (16,144 advanced AMD cases and 17,832 controls), and GERA study (4017 cases and 14,984 controls).
source: This meta-analysis also focussed on individuals with European ancestries and derived data from the IAMDGC 2013 (17,181 cases and 60,074 controls) (Fritsche et al., 2013) and IAMDGC 2016 (16,144 advanced AMD cases and 17,832 controls) (Fritsche et al., 2016) studies as well as the GERA study (4017 cases and 14,984 controls) (Kvale et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a description of the data source used in the study, citing multiple previous studies.

claim: Ceramide has been suggested as a causal factor in AMD through regulation of retinal cell death, inflammation, and neovascularisation.
source: Whilst sphingomyelin itself has not previously been described as a causative factor for AMD, other substances involved in sphingolipid metabolism (including ceramide, which can serve as both a substrate for sphingomyelin synthesis or a product of sphingomyelin metabolism) have been suggested as causal factors through regulation of retinal cell death, inflammation, and neovascularisation (Simon et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation.

claim: The balance of sphingolipids has crucial roles in determining cell fates.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Complement plays a key role in AMD pathogenesis.
